scope: Partial-accept rollback: skip LM-head on the accepted-prefix replay (task #4)
hardware: AMD Radeon 8060S / Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, Strix Halo APU, ~256 GB/s LPDDR5X)
change: verify_target_block(advance_state_only=True) skips the per-row LM-head vocab GEMV + greedy sampling on the accepted-prefix REPLAY (the replay only advances GDN linear + KV state; its tokens are already known from the first full-block pass and discarded). The bench reuses block_target_tokens[:consumed_rows]. Default behavior (no flag) for the replay path.

cost_breakdown_b5.command: instrumented scratchpad/rollback_cost.py, B5 24 cycles, 21 partial accepts

correctness.unit_test: tests/test_qwen35_gguf_verify_advance_state_only.py: committed linear state + FP32 hidden rows bit-identical to advance_state_only=False; reused first-pass tokens exact
correctness.e2e_token_stream: byte-identical across 20 B5 cycles (17 partial-accept) vs committed baseline

conclusion: The partial-accept rollback's reducible non-#10 overhead is the replay's discardable LM-head sampling (~16% of the replay forward); skipping it is exact and gives ~3.4% B5 cycle-time. The dominant rollback cost is the replay's layer-stack forward (~84%) which is the same GPU/bandwidth wall as #10 (confirms the task's original 'blocked by #10' framing for the bulk of the cost). The D2D state snapshot/restore is only ~1.8ms/cycle, not worth chasing. Eliminating the replay forward entirely would require per-row linear-state checkpointing inside the bulk GDN prefill (kernel surgery, O(rows) extra state memory) — deferred.
next_levers: #10 raise verifier layer-stack (MoE selected-expert GEMV) achieved bandwidth toward peak — the dominant rollback + verify cost
(deferred) per-row GDN linear-state checkpoint in the bulk prefill to remove the replay forward; net win only once the forward itself is cheaper
